row.key_detail: USPSTF grade A (2019) for: Pregnant women

official.topic: Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Pregnant Women: Screening
official.recommendation: The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in pregnant women at their first prenatal visit

row.question_original: I just found out I'm pregnant. Should I get screened for hepatitis B at my first prenatal visit?
user_turns: I just found out I'm pregnant. Should I get screened for hepatitis B at my first prenatal visit?
Okay. So bottom line: should I do it or not? Start your answer with exactly one of: DO IT / DON'T / IT DEPENDS.
replies:
Yes—**hepatitis B screening is recommended at your first prenatal visit during every pregnancy**, even if you’ve been vaccinated or tested negative before. It’s a routine blood test, usually for **hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)**.

Hepatitis B often causes no symptoms but can pass to a baby during birth. Finding it early lets your care team plan treatment if needed and protect your baby. If you test positive, your baby should receive the **hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth**, which is highly effective at preventing infection.

Ask your prenatal clinician to confirm that hepatitis B screening is included in your initial blood work.

DO IT — hepatitis B screening is recommended at your first prenatal visit during every pregnancy, even if you’re vaccinated or previously tested negative. It helps your care team protect you and your baby.
